He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]] and the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. ==High school career== Hardy began his high school career [[Southfield High School]], where he averaged 12 points per game as a freshman. He averaged 19 points per game as a sophomore but was limited to four games because of an MCL injury. Following his sophomore season, Hardy transferred to [[North Farmington High School]]. He averaged 21 points, four rebounds, six assists and six steals per game as a junior, helping the team reach the Class A state championship game. On January 20, 2017, Hardy scored 46 points in a 63–58 overtime loss to [[West Bloomfield High School]].{{cite news |last1=Purcell |first1=Jared |title=Meet Mr. Basketball finalist Amauri Hardy of North Farmington |url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/2017/03/meet_mr_basketball_finalist_am.html |access-date=December 26, 2021 |work=[[MLive]] |date=May 20, 2019}} As a senior, Hardy averaged 29 points, seven rebounds, six assists and six steals per game, helping the team finish 11–9. He was a finalist for the [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]] award.{{cite news |last1=Folsom |first1=Brandon |title=Mr. Basketball finalist Amauri Hardy became North Farmington's leader |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/03/16/mr-basketball-finalist-amauri-hardy-became-north-farmingtons-leader/99271406/ |access-date=December 26, 2021 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=March 16, 2017}} On December 9, 2016, Hardy initially committed to playing college basketball for [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] over [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]]. However, he reopened his recruitment after coach [[Brad Underwood]] left to take the job at [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], and committed to [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]] in April 2017.{{cite news |last1=Nelsen |first1=Chris |title=Former OSU commit Amauri Hardy signs with UNLV |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/osusportsextra/former-osu-commit-amauri-hardy-signs-with-unlv/article_b1c6e670-d12a-5fd1-a84c-8b4eef75ef09.html |access-date=December 26, 2021 |work=[[Tulsa World]] |date=April 28, 2017}} ==College career== Hardy averaged 5 points and 1.6 assists per game as a freshman.{{cite news |last1=Grimala |first1=Mike |title=Analysis: Early UNLV roster projection for 2019-20 |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2019/mar/08/analysis-early-unlv-roster-projection-for-2019-20/ |access-date=December 26, 2021 |work=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |date=March 8, 2019}} As a sophomore, Hardy averaged 13.1 points, 3.5 assists and 3 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=Oregon Ducks land four-star transfer guard Amauri Hardy |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/oregon-ducks/oregon-ducks-land-four-star-transfer-guard-amauri-hardy |access-date=December 26, 2021 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=April 12, 2020}} On November 9, 2019, he scored a career-high 27 points in a 60–56 overtime loss to [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]].{{cite web |title=Runnin' Rebels Fall In OT To Kansas State, 60–56 |url=https://unlvrebels.com/news/2019/11/9/mens-basketball-runnin-rebels-fall-in-ot-to-kansas-state-60-56.aspx |website=[[UNLV Runnin' Rebels]] |access-date=December 26, 2021 |date=November 9, 2019}} Hardy averaged 14.5 points, 3.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game as a junior, earning Third Team All-[[Mountain West Conference]] honors.{{cite news |last1=Nemec |first1=Andrew |title=Amauri Hardy, UNLV graduate transfer, officially signs with Oregon Ducks |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/2020/05/amauri-hardy-unlv-graduate-transfer-officially-signs-with-oregon-ducks.html |access-date=December 26, 2021 |work=[[The Oregonian]] |date=May 1, 2020}} He graduated and opted to transfer to [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], choosing the Ducks over [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]].{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Top-15 grad transfer Amauri Hardy commits to Oregon |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29026592/top-15-grad-transfer-amauri-hardy-commits-oregon |access-date=December 26, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 12, 2020}} As a senior, Hardy averaged 3.9 points and 2.2 assists per game. He made 13 starts while [[Will Richardson (basketball)|Will Richardson]] recovered from a thumb injury. Following the season, Hardy declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] and signed with an agent.{{cite magazine |last1=Reubenking |first1=Dylan |title=Amauri Hardy Declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/oregon/basketball/amauri-hardy-declares-for-2021-nba-draft |access-date=December 26, 2021 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=May 31, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===NBA G League Ignite (2021–2022)=== In September 2021, Hardy signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]], becoming the first college player to join the team.{{cite news |last1=Gordon |first1=Sam |title=Jaden and Amauri Hardy return to Las Vegas as teammates |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/basketball/jaden-and-amauri-hardy-return-to-las-vegas-as-teammates-2476148/ |access-date=December 26, 2021 |work=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |date=November 10, 2021}} He was suspended for breaking a team rule at the end of November.{{cite news |title=Amauri Hardy: Returns
